newsitem.title: USA: US spot MTBE slides with NYMEX gasoline in week.
newsitem.headline: US spot MTBE slides with NYMEX gasoline in week.

text.p: Spot MTBE prices were hit hard for the second consecutive week by NYMEX gasoline futures, which dove Wednesday on bearish fundamentals, players said on Thursday.
"MTBE goes down with gasoline but there is always a lag when gasoline goes back up," said a Houston-based trader, referring to gasoline's sharp rebound on Thursday.
In the Gulf Coast, spot Houston MTBE was pegged between 74.00 cents and 74.50 cents a gallon, 4.25 cents below last Thursday's values.
A 74.00 cent deal was heard done today, but it could not be confirmed. The last deal reported done was a 76.00 cent parcel Wednesday.
"We've seen prices in the sixties this time of year in the past," said Bill Richards, of DeWitt & Co. "But feedstocks are higher now than they were when MTBE prices were lower."
The market somewhat shrugged off news earlier in the week that Valero Energy Corp's long postponed $450 million project to produce MTBE in Mexico appears to have fallen through.

The project, a plant to produce 17,000 barrels daily of the gasoline additive, was put on hold first because of the Mexican economic crisis that followed that 1994 peso devaluation and later because of difficulties getting financing.
"The market is pretty well supplied already with MTBE. No one didn't really think the project would get the financing it needed," said a Houston-based producer.
Meanwhile, the Energy Information Administration said Thursday U.S. gasoline demand this summer is expected to rise to a record 8.14 million barrels per day, up 1.8 percent from last summer.

But traders said that refinery runs are at a quicker pace than last year and there is only a relatively minor deficit in supply, so prices are likely to be contained. -- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
